paper.title_en: Experimental demonstration of a multisigner quantum digital signature system
paper.abstract_en: Quantum digital signatures (QDSs) utilize shared keys generated by quantum key distribution, thereby providing information-theoretic security. Most existing QDS schemes, however, only support single-signer scenarios, which limits their applications in large-scale quantum networks. Based on previous studies of multisigner QDSs, we design and experimentally demonstrate a scalable multisigner QDS system. The results show that the designed system enables multiple signers to jointly sign the same message while supporting receiver verification and arbitrated validation. The single-photon count rate used in the experiment was approximately <math><mrow><mn>2.6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></math> counts/s. The measured coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) was greater than 830, and the second-order correlation function <math><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> was less than 0.01. The two-photon interference visibility measured for the polarization-entangled state <math><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mrow><mo>〉</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>〉</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>V</mi><mi>V</mi><mo>〉</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo></mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow></math> was approximately 99.01%, corresponding to a quantum bit error rate below 0.495%. This work demonstrates a reliable implementation of multisigner QDSs and may provide a practical approach to secure authentication and collaborative authorization in future large-scale quantum networks.
